knowledge:
- key_parameters: class=Specifies the BioPAX class (e.g., "pathway", "protein") to filter instances in listInstances or selectInstances ;; id=The unique identifier of a BioPAX instance used to retrieve properties or components ;; expandSubpathways=Logical parameter in pathway2AdjacancyMatrix to determine whether to expand nested subpathways ;; splitComplexMolecules=Logical parameter in pathway2AdjacancyMatrix and pathway2RegulatoryGraph to split complex molecules into their atomic members so they share the same edges ;; layoutGraph=Logical parameter in plotRegulatoryGraph to control whether to apply a layout before plotting
- alternatives: None mentioned, though the documentation notes that users can layout and plot graphs themselves instead of using the built-in Rgraphviz-based layoutRegulatoryGraph and plotRegulatoryGraph functions.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have biological pathway data in BioPAX format (Level 2 or Level 3) and want to programmatically query, modify, visualize, or convert these pathways into regulatory networks/graphs in R.
- pitfalls: Regulatory graphs rely solely on BioPAX activation and inhibition information from the "control" class; a lack of this information will lead to disconnected or incomplete graphs. Parsing very large BioPAX files (like Reactome) is highly resource-intensive and can take up to an hour. System-level prerequisites (libxml2, libcurl, and graphviz for older Rgraphviz versions) must be installed on the operating system prior to package installation.

workflows.name: parse_and_visualize_biopax
workflows.intent: Parse an existing BioPAX OWL file, extract a specific pathway, convert it to a regulatory graph, and visualize it.
input: file.owl (BioPAX OWL file containing pathway data)
workflows.stages: 1. Parse the BioPAX file into R. 2. List and select pathway instances. 3. Convert the selected pathway to a regulatory graph and adjacency matrix. 4. Layout and plot the regulatory graph.
workflows.code:
biopax = readBiopax(file)
print(biopax)
pw_list = listInstances(biopax, class="pathway")
pw_complete = selectInstances(biopax, class="pathway")
pwid1 = "pid_p_100002_wntpathway"
getInstanceProperty(biopax, pwid1, property="NAME")
pw_1 = selectInstances(biopax, class="pathway", id=pwid1)
pw_1_component_list = listPathwayComponents(biopax,pwid1)
pw_1_components = selectInstances(biopax,id=pw_1_component_list$id)
pw_1_adj = pathway2AdjacancyMatrix(biopax, pwid1, expandSubpathways=TRUE, splitComplexMolecules=TRUE, verbose=TRUE)
pw_1_graph = pathway2RegulatoryGraph(biopax, pwid1, splitComplexMolecules=TRUE, verbose=TRUE)
pw_1_graph_laidout = layoutRegulatoryGraph(pw_1_graph)
plotRegulatoryGraph(pw_1_graph)

workflows.name: create_and_modify_biopax
workflows.intent: Programmatically build a new BioPAX model from scratch, add physical entities, biochemical reactions, controls, and pathways, and write the model to an OWL file.
workflows.stages: 1. Initialize a new BioPAX object. 2. Add physical entities, participants, and biochemical reactions. 3. Add control interactions (activations/inhibitions). 4. Define pathways and merge them. 5. Write the model to an OWL file.
workflows.code:
biopax = createBiopax()
for(i in LETTERS[1:5]) {
	biopax = addPhysicalEntity(biopax, class="protein",
		NAME=paste("protein",i,sep="_"), 
		id=paste("proteinid",i,sep="_"))
	biopax = addPhysicalEntityParticipant(biopax,
		referencedPhysicalEntityID=paste("proteinid",i,sep="_"), 
		id=paste("PEPid",i,sep="_"))
	biopax = addBiochemicalReaction(biopax, LEFT=paste("PEPid",i,sep="_"),
		RIGHT=paste("PEPid",i,sep="_"),
		id=paste("BCRid",i,sep="_"))
}
biopax = addControl(biopax, CONTROL_TYPE="ACTIVATION",
	CONTROLLER="PEPid_A", CONTROLLED=c("BCRid_B"),id="control_1")
biopax = addControl(biopax, CONTROL_TYPE="INHIBITION",
	CONTROLLER="PEPid_A", CONTROLLED=c("BCRid_C"),id="control_2")
biopax = addControl(biopax, CONTROL_TYPE="ACTIVATION",
	CONTROLLER="PEPid_C", CONTROLLED=c("BCRid_D"),id="control_3")
biopax = addControl(biopax, CONTROL_TYPE="INHIBITION",
	CONTROLLER="PEPid_C", CONTROLLED=c("BCRid_E"), id="control_4")
biopax = addPathway(biopax, NAME="pw1",
	PATHWAY_COMPONENTS=c("control_1","control_2"), id="pwid1")
biopax = addPathway(biopax, NAME="pw2",
	PATHWAY_COMPONENTS=c("control_3","control_4"), id="pwid2")
biopax = mergePathways(biopax, "pwid1", "pwid2", NAME="pw3", id="pwid3")
writeBiopax(biopax, file="test.writeBiopax.owl")
